findings.note: The transactional crash-safety invariant is not implemented on a supported platform: `_fsync_directory` immediately returns whenever `os.name != "posix"`, and the adjacent implementation text explicitly characterizes rename/unlink durability hardening as POSIX-only. The bundle also states that the `.ps1` twin runs on Windows CI, yet contains no Windows-specific durability primitive or evidence establishing equivalent ordering there. Consequently, on Windows the journal rename, staging-chain creation, publication renames, rollback unlinks, and pre-discard recovery state can proceed without the directory durability barriers that the implementation itself says prevent a hard crash from leaving an undetected mixed generation, so AC-047's platform-unqualified recovery guarantee is not met.

The captured mutation proof shows mutant O, which removes the directory fsync after restoring an `ABSENT` PRE state by unlinking, still passing at the clean-control tally of 395/0. The capture attributes this to `plant_sentinels` making every publication artifact pre-exist and explicitly labels the necessary omitted-PRE fixture as open work. Thus the POSIX implementation contains the intended barrier, but the security-sensitive regression suite cannot detect its removal on this rollback branch.
